title: Bundle ZXing (or pin it with SRI) and fix sign-out edge cases before real users sign in
description: From the security review of PR #47. (1) Medium: src/index.html loads @zxing/library 0.21.3 from cdn.jsdelivr.net with no integrity attribute, and the CSP allows script-src https://cdn.jsdelivr.net (whole host). The script runs before the app, and the app origin now holds bearer tokens, so a compromised CDN path could read ?code/?invite tokens, wrap fetch/WebSocket, and mint tokens via /auth/refresh. Fix: bundle @zxing/library from npm through Vite (preferred) and drop jsdelivr from script-src; or add SRI + crossorigin and narrow script-src to the exact package path. (2) Low: sign-out doesn't clear the saved invite in sessionStorage (supplyCheckout.invite). (3) Low: a failed POST /auth/sign-out is swallowed and the page redirects anyway, leaving the refresh cookie valid; only redirect on success, else show an error. (4) Hardening: session.js refresh timer with a missing expiresIn gives NaN; default to 3600. (5) Hardening: db.js colls[ev.collection] should use Object.hasOwn.
acceptance_criteria: No third-party script without SRI; CSP script-src has no whole-CDN host; tests for sign-out clearing the invite and for a failed sign-out not redirecting; the artifact build still works in claude.ai.

title: Add atomic, idempotent checkout, return and stock-adjust commands with an inventory movement log
description: Today a checkout saves the sheet line and then bumps stock in a separate read-then-write (src/main.js bumpStock), so a retry or double tap can decrement stock twice, concurrent checkouts on one line can lose a count, and there is no inventory history for the planned stock-drift alarm (docs/journeys.md J4). Add server commands next to the generic document routes (which the edit screens keep using): checkout, return and stock adjust. Each is one DynamoDB transaction that updates the sheet line (server-side ADD on out/returned), stock, a movement record and an operation-ID record; a retry with the same operation ID returns the first result. Server validates integer quantities, returned <= out, prices >= 0 and closed-sheet rules. IAM: add UpdateItem and ConditionCheckItem under the existing LeadingKeys condition. Per-item stock history view. The claude.ai artifact build keeps its two-write path (ADR 0004); this extends ADR 0006 with commands.
acceptance_criteria: Retrying the same operation changes nothing (test); a failure mid-operation leaves nothing half-saved (test); concurrent checkouts on one line never lose a count (test); the nightly drift check can reconcile stock against movements.

title: Clear local session data when the session ends without Sign out
description: When a refresh 401 shows the sign-in screen (expired session, or a sign-out that timed out client-side but succeeded server-side), supplyCheckout.team and the receipt draft stay in localStorage on shared devices (PR #61 review). Clear them when a different user signs in (store the owner sub with the draft) or on onSignedOut.
acceptance_criteria: After a session ends via a refresh 401 and a different user signs in, they never see the previous user's team choice or receipt draft; tests cover it.

title: Let users switch between light, dark and system themes
description: styles.css already defines dark tokens under prefers-color-scheme and :root[data-theme=dark|light], but nothing in the app sets data-theme. Add a theme control (System / Light / Dark) that sets data-theme on <html>, remembers the choice per device in localStorage (wrapped in try/catch so it works when storage throws), and applies it before first paint to avoid a flash. title: Finish sign-out hardening: clear the receipt draft, block refreshes while signing out, and time out requests
description: From the PR #58 review (all Low). (1) signOut (src/aws/session.js ~106) doesn't clear localStorage supplyCheckout.receiptDraft, so the next person to sign in on a shared device sees the previous user's receipt draft (names, prices, vendor, product keys, sheet IDs). Clear it on sign-out; longer term key the draft by team. (2) A refresh started during the sign-out POST (a 401 from a live-event fetch) can rotate the cookie after the revoke; add a signingOut flag so refresh() rejects while signing out, cleared on failure. (3) src/aws/http.js fetch has no timeout, so a stalled refresh stalls sign-out with no feedback; give request() a default AbortSignal.timeout(15000) and disable the sign-out button while it runs.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: the draft is cleared on sign-out; a 401-triggered refresh during sign-out doesn't run; a stalled request times out and sign-out reports an error.

title: Stop in-flight token refreshes on sign-out and tidy sign-out leftovers
description: From the PR #55 review. Low: signOut (src/aws/session.js ~92-97) can race a /auth/refresh already in flight; with refresh-token rotation a refresh response landing after sign-out's cookie clear could leave a fresh refresh cookie, silently signing the user back in. Fix: at the top of signOut, clearTimeout(timer) and await any in-flight refresh before POST /auth/sign-out. Info: also clear localStorage supplyCheckout.team on sign-out; tighten CSP worker-src to 'self' or 'none' (no workers are used).
acceptance_criteria: Test: sign-out during an in-flight refresh leaves the user signed out on reload; team key cleared; CSP worker-src tightened with its test updated.

title: Use own-property lookups for item keys in the app's receipt save and inventory
description: From the PR #53 review. src/main.js (~684) builds items = {} then items[k] || (items[k] = ...); for a barcode whose keyOf() is 'constructor' or 'toString' this finds the built-in function, drops the line silently and sets a stray .out on the built-in. Check products[k] lookups and items[k].code (~401) too. Fix with Object.hasOwn, Object.create(null) or Map. keyOf('__proto__') gives '__proto__', which the backend now refuses with 400; show a clear message or map it to a safe key.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: a receipt with barcodes that key to constructor, toString and __proto__ saves correctly or with a clear message, in both builds; no built-in object is modified.

title: Handle built-in object names as product keys in the checkout commands, and oversized sheets
description: From the post-merge security review of PR #49. (1) Low: commands.ts looks lines up with items?.[key] and builds {[key]: line}; keys.ts accepts __proto__, constructor, toString. With __proto__ the SDK marshall drops the line but the transaction commits (version bump, movement, stock decrement), so stock moves with no line; constructor/toString resolve to functions, so such products can't be added to a sheet that has items. Fix: Object.hasOwn lookups at commands.ts ~357 and ~461, reject __proto__ in productKey() like checkValue does, build :items without prototype assignment; tests for __proto__ and constructor. (2) Info: commands skip the 350 KB document size check; past 400 KB DynamoDB cancels with ValidationError, which becomes a 500. Map that cancellation on the sheet item to 413 quota_exceeded (TooLargeError) and optionally estimate the new line's size first.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: __proto__ is refused as a product key; a product keyed constructor or toString can be checked out onto a sheet that already has items; an oversized sheet gives 413, not 500.

title: Run the DynamoDB Local tests locally
description: Docker isn't running on the dev laptop, so the DynamoDB Local tests only run in CI, adding a push-and-wait loop. Add npm run test:ddb in backend/ that starts amazon/dynamodb-local with Docker or colima when available, runs the suites and stops it, and document installing colima (the owner installs it).
acceptance_criteria: npm run test:ddb runs the DynamoDB Local suites locally when a container runtime is installed, and explains how to install one otherwise.

title: Make refreshing the beads export a one-command chore PR

Add a script (for example npm run beads:pr) that exports, opens a chore PR if anything changed, and lands it; drop the per-land warning in favour of running it after a batch of merges. The beads database is local, so this can't run in CI.
acceptance_criteria: One command refreshes the export through a PR; land no longer warns every time.

title: Set email_verified for Google and Apple sign-ins from the provider's own claim
description: PR #40 removed the emailVerified mapping from the Google and Apple providers, because Cognito requires IdP-mapped attributes to be client-writable and email_verified must not be. Federated users therefore start unverified and can't see or accept invites. Add a Cognito trigger (post confirmation or pre token generation) that reads the provider's verified-email claim and sets email_verified with AdminUpdateUserAttributes, only when the provider says the email is verified.
acceptance_criteria: A Google or Apple user whose provider email is verified can see and accept invites; one whose provider email isn't verified can't (tests); the web client still can't write email_verified.

title: Cut off live updates for removed members and canceled teams within about a minute
description: AppSync Events can't end or filter an open subscription server-side, so a removed member's open connection keeps receiving change notices (collection, ID, op, version; product IDs can be barcodes or names) until it closes: up to 24 h, or under an hour if the client reconnects on token refresh as the contract says. Options from docs/api/realtime.md: per-member channels /users/<sub> with the consumer caching membership for about 60 s (one publish per member per change; departs from ADR 0006), or a rotating team channel /teams/<id>/<epoch> that member removal and billing rotate. Decide and build one. Document contents are already protected by the API's membership check.
acceptance_criteria: A removed member or a canceled team's members receive no further change notices within about 60 s of the change (test).

title: Set one-year log retention on the API functions' log groups

acceptance_criteria: Every log group in every stack has one-year retention (assertion test).

title: Make npm run land explain a blocked PR and fail when it can't merge
